Object Deep Merge Behavior

Object Deep Merge is a Merge behavior that combines object-based FeatureCell state values by recursively merging nested plain-object structures during the Merge stage.

This behavior treats objects as immutable values. When both the current state and the incoming value are plain objects, a deep, recursive merge is performed, producing a new object that incorporates nested updates without mutating existing state.

Non-plain-object values—including primitives, arrays, null, and class instances—are replaced directly rather than merged. This ensures predictable structural behavior and avoids unintended traversal of non-object data.

Object Deep Merge runs within the core Merge stage and produces the merged candidate state passed to downstream pipeline stages. It does not mutate existing state, does not emit snapshots directly, and does not influence pipeline control flow beyond producing the merged value.

Note

The Merge stage is entered exclusively through explicit state-update APIs. Pipeline executions that invoke merge semantics are initiated via the mergeState methods, which supply the incoming value and optional merge configuration used by the active Merge behavior.

Diagram
Configuration

Object deep merge behavior is configured as part of the Merge stage and defines how object-based FeatureCell state values are combined with incoming resolved values using recursive, structural merge semantics.

Exactly one merge behavior is active for a FeatureCell at any time. When withObjectDeepMergeBehavior is provided, it replaces the default merge strategy and becomes the active merge behavior for that FeatureCell.

Merge behaviors may be influenced by the clearUndefined configuration flag. When clearUndefined is enabled, an incoming undefined value is treated as an intentional clear request and results in the FeatureCell state being cleared. When disabled, incoming undefined values preserve the existing state and produce no merge output.

Object Deep Merge also supports the stripNulls configuration option. When enabled, properties with null values are removed from the merged result after recursive merging is complete. This allows intentional field removal without replacing the entire object structure.

The clearUndefined and stripNulls options are supplied at the time a merge-style update is initiated and are evaluated by the active merge behavior during the Merge stage. These options do not affect resolution, operators, or downstream pipeline stages.

Object deep merge recursively combines nested plain-object structures. Non-plain objects—including primitives, arrays, null, and class instances—are replaced directly rather than merged. Existing state is never mutated, and all merged results are produced as new immutable objects.

Evaluation Outcomes

The Object Deep Merge behavior evaluates the current committed FeatureCell state and the incoming resolved value to produce a single merged result during the Merge stage.

When both the current state and incoming value are plain objects, Object Deep Merge recursively combines nested properties. Existing nested fields are preserved unless explicitly replaced by the incoming value.

Non-object values—including primitives, arrays, null, and class instances—are replaced directly rather than merged. No mutation of existing state occurs.

When the incoming value is undefined, merge behavior is controlled by the clearUndefined configuration option. This determines whether the existing state is preserved or intentionally cleared. Optional stripNulls configuration may also remove null fields from the merged result.

Example 1: Recursive Object Merge
Inputs Merged Result
current: { user: { id: 1, name: "Jane" } }

next: { user: { name: "Jane Doe" } }

 { user: { id: 1, name: "Jane Doe" } } — nested objects are merged recursively
Example 2: Replace Non-Plain Object
Inputs Merged Result
current: { count: 5 }

next: 9

 9 — non-object value replaces the existing state
Example 3: Strip Null Fields
Inputs Merged Result
current: { user: { id: 1, name: "Jane" } }

next: { user: { name: null } }

stripNulls: true

 { user: { id: 1 } } — null fields are removed after merge
Example 4: Undefined Incoming Value (Preserve)
Inputs Merged Result
current: { enabled: true }

next: undefined

clearUndefined: false

 { enabled: true } — existing state is preserved
Example 5: Undefined Incoming Value (Clear)
Inputs Merged Result
current: { enabled: true }

next: undefined

clearUndefined: true

 undefined — state is intentionally cleared
Examples

Example 1: Use the withObjectDeepMergeBehavior in a FeatureCell

This example demonstrates a FeatureCell configured with the withObjectDeepMergeBehavior. Instead of replacing the entire state object, incoming values provided via mergeState are recursively merged into the existing state, preserving unaffected nested properties.

By explicitly attaching the Object Deep Merge behavior, the FeatureCell adopts deep, structural merge semantics during the Merge stage. This makes it suitable for hierarchical or patch-style state updates where only a subset of nested fields change over time.

Note

When a custom merge behavior is supplied, it replaces the default withArrayMergeBehavior for that FeatureCell. Exactly one merge behavior is active at any time. 

{{`// app.config.ts

export const appConfig: ApplicationConfig = {
  providers: [
    provideVault({ logLevel: 'off' }),

    provideFeatureCell(
      EmployeeService
      {
        key: 'employee-profile',
        initialState: {
          user: {
            id: 1,
            name: 'Jane',
            preferences: {
              theme: 'light'
            }
          }
        }
      },
      [
        // Explicitly attach the Object Deep Merge behavior
        withObjectDeepMergeBehavior
      ]
    )
  ]
};

// bank-employee.service.ts

import { Injectable } from '@angular/core';
import { FeatureCell, injectVault } from '@sdux-vault/angular';
import { EmployeeProfile } from './employee-profile.shape';

@FeatureCell<EmployeeProfile>('employee-profile')
@Injectable({ providedIn: 'root' })
export class EmployeeService {
  readonly vault = injectVault<EmployeeProfile>(EmployeeService);

  constructor() {
    this.vault.initialize();
  }

  updateEmployeeName(): void {
    this.vault.mergeState({
      value: {
        user: {
          name: 'Jane Doe'
        }
      }
    });
  }
}`}}
 
{{`export const employeeCell = FeatureCell<EmployeeProfile>(
  {
    key: 'employee-profile',
    initialState: {
      user: {
        id: 1,
        name: 'Jane',
        preferences: {
          theme: 'light'
        }
      }
    },
  },
  [
    // Explicitly attach the Object Deep Merge behavior
    withObjectDeepMergeBehavior
  ]
);

// Initialize the FeatureCell
employeeCell.initialize();

// Deep-merge a nested update
employeeCell.mergeState({
  value: {
    user: {
      name: 'Jane Doe'
    }
  }
});`}}
